 Preview: November 19 vs. Montreal
 Canes look to extend their win streak to five
 By 
 Walt Ruff & Peter Dewar 
 Hurricanes.com 
 November 19, 2026 
 Link copied 
 RALEIGH, N.C. - The Carolina Hurricanes host their annual Hockey Fights Cancer game presented by UNC Health, on Thursday, taking on the Montreal Canadiens.
 ---
 When: Thursday, November 19
 Where: Lenovo Center
 Puck Drop: 7:00 p.m. ET
 How To Watch: Hurricanes Hockey Network| Full Broadcast Info 
 Listen: 99.9 The Fan, Hurricanes App
 ---
 Canes Record: 16-3-2 (34 Points - 1st, Metropolitan Division)
 Canes Last Game: 5-1 Win over the Seattle Kraken on Saturday, Nov. 14
 ---
 Canadiens Record: 13-5-4 (30 Points - T-2nd, Atlantic Division)
 Canadiens Last Game: 3-2 Win over the New Jersey Devils on Wednesday, Nov. 18
 Gameday Central
 Get ready for your trip to Lenovo Center with the Canes' gameday hub! Find out when doors/lots open, purchase parking, check out activations and more.
 Click Here 
 Last Time Out...
 The Canes completed their two-game Global Series sweep of the Kraken on Saturday, taking a convincing 5-1 win .
 Driven by three power-play goals, both  Mark Jankowski  and Andrei Svechnikov  each had a pair of goals themselves.
 Pyotr Kochetkov had a light day of work in net, needing to make just 12 saves for his 12th win of the season.
 Previous Meetings vs. MTL This Season...
 Oct. 6 : The Canes won a back-and-forth battle at Bell Centre, 6-4.
 Blaker's Rolling...
 Forward Jackson Blake enters today's game with a career-best 11-game point streak (5G, 8A).
 With at least one point in each contest dating back to Oct. 20, the third-year pro sits tied for second on the team with 21 points in 21 games.
 His point streak is currently tied for the second-longest in the NHL this season, behind Connor McDavid's 22-game run.
 In Net...
 With four days since their last game, the Canes have the option of going with either Brandon Bussi or Pyotr Kochetkov  this evening.
 Kochetkov was in the crease usually occupied by the next day's starter at Wednesday's practice, perhaps signaling that he'll be in line to try and add to his 12-1 start.
 Should they decide to go the other way, Bussi is 4-1-1 in his last six starts, including a win over Montreal on Oct. 6.
 On The Other Side...
 Montreal arrives in Raleigh on the latter half of a back-to-back after knocking off New Jersey 3-2 last night.
 Lane Hutson picked up assists on all three goals in that victory and leads his team with 22 points on the year. His 19 total helpers are the 7th-most by an NHL blueliner this season.
 With Jacob Fowler starting last night at Prudential Center, it is likely that Jakub Dobes will have the net this evening. Dobes had a breakout 2025-26 season, but a sluggish start allowed Fowler to take the reins. Having won two of his last three, the 25-year-old will look to continue turning a corner tonight.

 Injury Updates...
 No injuries to report at the moment.
 What Are We Wearing?
 The Canes will wear their BLACK uniforms. To view the full home uniform schedule, click here .
 What's Next After This Game?
 The Canes are scheduled to practice on Friday. They'll return to game action on Saturday afternoon against the Edmonton Oilers.
